svg.title: Local Git cheat sheet, illustrated
svg.desc: Twenty-four illustrated cards, colour-coded by group. Start and check: git init turns a folder into a repository with a hidden .git; git status shows what changed; git diff shows removed lines in red and added lines in green, press q to leave. Commit: git add -A puts all changes in the envelope; git commit -m with a note seals it and files it in the cabinet. Branches: git switch -c experiment/x starts a side track; git switch main moves you back to main; git branch lists the branches, with a star where you are; git merge --no-edit experiment/x brings a branch into main; git branch -d experiment/x deletes a merged branch. History: git log --oneline --graph --all shows the whole history; git log --oneline -- report.md shows a file's history; git restore --source with an id brings an old version of a file back. Undo: git restore report.md throws away edits, with no undo; git restore --staged report.md takes a file out of the envelope; git reset --soft HEAD~1 unseals the last commit and keeps your edits; git revert --no-edit with an id adds a commit that cancels an old one. Backup: git bundle create x.bundle --all packs everything into one file; git push --all backup tops up the spare cabinet. Windows: gitk --all draws the history; git gui commits with buttons. Tips: the daily loop is edit, status, add, commit; survival keys are q to leave and right-click to paste; golden rule: no reset --hard and no force push.
svg.text: Every command from this guide, in one picture. Copy them from the table below it.
